scope: Desktop widget/opaque-display/lifecycle regression, not native secure VM, in-game taint, pixels, latency, CPU, memory/allocation or FPS acceptance. Baseline lacks the feature and its new regressions fail, so process times are not comparable performance evidence.
scenario: Highest screen top then left across native and explicitly enabled owned Threat; native opaque SetText forwarding; native alpha/cache retirement; Threat-only observed-combat fallback with target, fight, hide and cleanup lifecycle; 500 reuse cycles.
configuration: Lua 5.4.6 fresh fixture process per sample. Five alternating baseline/candidate pairs. Ordinary clock polls reuse the existing Threat 0.2s driver; no new ticker or native configuration calls.
warmup: Each bounded script initializes module/widgets before its repeated loop; no additional warmup. Raw process wall time includes startup.
resourceCost: One owned Threat FontString and at most one permanent guarded SetText posthook per native session timer; bounded cache per native window. Owned visibility hooks reuse the timer hook set. No new frames, events or tickers. Inactive hooks return without text forwarding.
nativeStatus: Pending controlled fresh reload, actual actor/secret/taint/menu/appearance/combat tests. No game input, profiler or SavedVariables changes by this worker.
fallbackLimits: Threat-only timer is ordinary elapsed time for observed player-combat intervals, cleared on combat exit/hide. Revealing mid-combat starts at first observation; no unseen start or native historical duration is invented. Native mirrors become current on their next natural SetText; no GetText/manual Refresh bootstrap.
